newsitem.title: FRANCE: Morocco's Basri slams France over visa red tape.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Basri slams France over visa red tape.

text.p: Moroccan Interior Minister Driss Basri on Saturday accused French authorities of using bureaucratic harassment to discourage Moroccan visitors as part of crackdown on illegal immigration.

In a sharp attack on France's controversial immigration policies, Basri said he told French President Jacques Chirac that Morocco could no longer accept such practices, which harmed bilateral economic and cultural relations.

He said French authorities were asking Moroccans applying for a visitor's visa to provide bank guarantees, certificates stating where they would stay in France and evidence that they would return home.
"They are being made to wait, then they do not get a visa," he told a news conference at the Moroccan ambassador's residence.
"I have told President Chirac that it was regrettable that we reached such a situation...We can no longer accept it, it's a matter of principle," he said.
"On the one hand they speak about rapprochement, on the other they shut the door," he said.
He said Paris and Rabat would set up a joint commission to try to find solutions to the problem.
Basri was in Paris for a meeting of interior ministers from the western Mediterranean on drugs, terrorism and immigration.

He would not be drawn into criticising hardline French immigration laws. But he said that for the sake of curbing illegal immigration, Paris was also hampering legal immigration and bona fide visits by relatives of members of France's Moroccan community, including business people and scholars.
"France will lose out, they are going to Germany and the United States instead," he said.

Moroccan writer Tahar Ben Jelloun, a winner of France's top Goncourt literary prize, recently wrote in the daily Le Monde that his mother had stopped visiting him in France because of the red tape involved.
In an effort to stop the rise of Jean-Marie Le Pen's far-right, anti-immigrant National Front, the centre-right government has cracked down on immigration since coming to power four years ago.

A new law last month laid down increasingly tough conditions for immigrants, prompting protests by artists, intellectuals and left-wingers who accuse Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre of pandering to the Front, which advocates sending all immigrants home.
